title: Finite cohomological dimension bounds the unbounded derived functor from above
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], and suppose $\mathcal A$ has enough injectives, meaning every object embeds in an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and left exact, with right derived functors $R^qF$ on objects [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Fix an integer $N\geq0$ and assume $R^qF(A)=0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$ and every $q>N$. Use unbounded cochain derived categories and their cohomology functors [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then the total right derived functor $RF:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ exists. For every integer $t$ and every $E\in D(\mathcal A)$ with $H^i(E)=0$ for all $i>t$, one has $H^i(RF(E))=0$ for all $i>t+N$.

source.place: Tag 07K7, lemma-unbounded-right-derived, (1) and (4)(c), with n=N+1 and interval [-infinity,t]; source read at /home/ubuntu/weil-launcher-nt/literature/stacks-project/derived.tex:9977-10109.

proof.text: Put $d(A)=\max(\{0\}\cup\{q>0:R^qF(A)\ne0\})$. The maximum exists and is at most $N$ by hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing], injectives have degree zero; enough injectives therefore provides every required degree-zero embedding. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] to $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$. If $q>\max\{d(A)-1,d(B)\}$, then $q>0$, $R^qF(B)=0$, and $R^{q+1}F(A)=0$, so exactness forces $R^qF(C)=0$. Hence $d(C)\leq\max\{d(A)-1,d(B)\}$ (truncated subtraction). Applied to $0\to A\to A\oplus B\to B\to0$, the same long exact sequence gives $d(A\oplus B)\leq\max\{d(A),d(B)\}$. Thus all hypotheses of the bounded degree-function replacement lemma hold, including for $N=0$.

source.place: Tag 07K7, lemma-unbounded-right-derived, second proof paragraph: degree function and verification of the hypotheses of 07K6.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-degree-zero-complex-replacement] with $D=N$ and the function in Step 1. Every complex $K$ is consequently the source of a quasi-isomorphism $K\to L$ with $R^qF(L^r)=0$ for every $q>0$ and $r\in\mathbf Z$. Call these complexes termwise $F$-acyclic, and let $\mathcal I$ be their class. There is no bound on the cochain degrees of $K$ or $L$.

source.place: Tags 07K6 (lemma-replace-resolution) and 07K7, construction of termwise right-acyclic replacements.

proof.text: The existing [lem-kun-pointwise-finite-cd-exact-complex] applies with a singleton indexing set, $r_*=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal B}$ and $d_*=N$. The identity functor preserves monomorphisms, and the singleton identity family detects zero objects; its required pointwise vanishing is exactly the assumption $R^qF(A)=0$ for $q>N$. Therefore, if a termwise $F$-acyclic complex $T$ is exact, then $F(T)$ is exact. Only enough injectives in $\mathcal A$ is used by this cited statement; no Grothendieck hypothesis is introduced.

source.place: Tag 07K7, quasi-isomorphism preservation claim, using its finite-dimension shifting argument in the existing pointwise exact-complex lemma.

proof.text: Let $s:L\to M$ be a quasi-isomorphism between members of $\mathcal I$. Its cone is exact by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic]. Its terms are $M^r\oplus L^{r+1}$, and these are $F$-acyclic: in the long exact sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] for $0\to M^r\to M^r\oplus L^{r+1}\to L^{r+1}\to0$, both outer objects in each positive derived degree vanish. Step 3 gives that $F(\operatorname{Cone}(s))$ is exact. Because $F$ is additive, its canonical finite-biproduct identification carries the cone differential matrix to $\begin{pmatrix}F(d_M)&F(s)\\0&-F(d_L)\end{pmatrix}$, so $F(\operatorname{Cone}(s))\cong\operatorname{Cone}(F(s))$. Applying the same cone criterion in $\mathcal B$ proves that $F(s)$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic, and Tag 07K7, quasi-isomorphism preservation claim.

proof.text: Let $G:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ send a complex $K$ to $Q_{\mathcal B}(F(K))$. For a homotopy $f-g=d_Mh+hd_K$, additivity gives $F(f)-F(g)=F(d_M)F(h)+F(h)F(d_K)$; hence $G$ is defined on the homotopy category. The identity $F(-d_K)=-F(d_K)$ identifies $F(K[1])$ with $F(K)[1]$. Step 4 identifies the cone differentials, and additivity preserves the cone inclusion and the signed projection. Thus termwise $F$ carries cone triangles to cone triangles. By [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated], these triangles and their isomorphic copies are precisely the distinguished triangles in $K(\mathcal A)$, and $Q_{\mathcal B}$ is exact. Consequently $G$ is exact. Step 2 gives right replacements by $\mathcal I$, and Step 4 shows that $G$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms between its members. The criterion [lem-sf-right-derived-from-adapted-complexes] gives the unbounded total right derived functor $RF$ and, for every $L\in\mathcal I$, the computation $RF(Q_{\mathcal A}L)\cong Q_{\mathcal B}F(L)$. This establishes existence on all of $D(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: Tag 06XN, lemma-find-existence-computes, applied as in the proof of 07K7 (1)-(2).

proof.text: Represent $E$ by $L\in\mathcal I$ via Step 2; then $H^r(L)=0$ for $r>t$. Put $Z^r=\ker(d_L^r)$. For every $r\geq t$, exactness at degree $r+1$ gives $0\to Z^r\to L^r\to Z^{r+1}\to0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] and the positive-degree acyclicity of $L^r$, its connecting morphisms give $R^pF(Z^{r+1})\cong R^{p+1}F(Z^r)$ for $p\geq1$. Since $F$ preserves kernels, the cycles of $F(L)$ at $i$ are $F(Z^i)$. The degree-zero start of the same long exact sequence, with $R^0F\cong F$ from [lem-sp-derived-well-defined], identifies $H^i(F(L))=\operatorname{coker}(F(L^{i-1})\to F(Z^i))\cong R^1F(Z^{i-1})$ whenever $i>t$. If $i>t+N$, iterate the displayed connecting isomorphisms $N$ times to obtain $R^1F(Z^{i-1})\cong R^{N+1}F(Z^{i-N-1})=0$. Every sequence used has index $r\geq i-N-1\geq t$; when $N=0$ no iteration is needed and the vanishing is $R^1F=0$. Finally Step 5 computes $H^i(RF(E))$ as $H^i(F(L))$, proving the asserted bound.

Proved degree-function conditions, supplied 07K6 replacements, reused the existing pointwise exact-complex result to verify quasi-isomorphism preservation, and used 06XN to derive globally. Proved the bound by explicit finite dimension shifting of cycles; no bounded-below spectral sequence or unbounded K-injective existence hypothesis is assumed. Two strictly smaller, statement-only tools are new.
